findings.title: Stop signal causes queued jobs to be abandoned instead of drained
findings.evidence: The main loop exits immediately once the stop event is set, so any jobs already present in the source queue but not yet pulled are never submitted, despite the class docstring promising drain-before-exit behavior.
findings.recommendation: Clarify the contract to only drain already-submitted work, or change the loop to continue consuming already-queued items after stop is requested, for example by draining the queue with non-blocking gets until it is empty before leaving the executor context.

findings.title: Invalid max_workers value now crashes the worker at startup
findings.evidence: The constructor accepts max_workers unchecked and passes it directly into ThreadPoolExecutor, which raises ValueError for 0 or negative values, causing run() to fail immediately on a reachable configuration path.
findings.recommendation: Validate max_workers in __init__ and reject non-positive values with a clear error, or coerce to a safe minimum such as 1 before constructing the executor.
